findings.source_quote: ὅτε οὖν ἐνεδυναμώθης διὰ τοῦ πνεύματος καὶ ἴσχυσας τῇ ἰσχύϊ σου, ὥστε δύνασθαί σε καὶ ἄγγελον ἰδεῖν
findings.english_quote: When you were strengthened through the Spirit and grew strong enough even to see an angel
findings.issue: The rendering absorbs the result clause into “strong enough” and leaves τῇ ἰσχύϊ σου, “in your strength,” without explicit representation. This loses the source’s repeated strength wording and its second-person possessive alongside strengthening through the Spirit.
findings.suggested_revision: Consider: “When you were strengthened through the Spirit and grew strong in your strength, so that you could even see an angel”. Review this candidate afresh for intelligibility and fidelity without explaining away the source’s repetition.

findings.source_quote: Μετὰ τὸ γράψαι με τὰς ἐντολὰς καὶ παραβολὰς τοῦ ποιμένος, τοῦ ἀγγέλου τῆς μετανοίας, ἦλθε πρὸς με καὶ λέγει μοι· Θέλω σοι δεῖξαι ὅσα σοι ἔδειξε τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον τὸ λαλῆσαν μετὰ σοῦ ἐν μορφῇ τῆς Ἐκκλησίας· ἐκεῖνο γὰρ τὸ πνεῦμα ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ Θεοῦ ἐστίν.
findings.english_quote: Retain both invited groups, the response conditions, suffering without supplied willingness, and the explicit Spirit/Son statement.
findings.issue: The unit’s theological metadata mixes its actual Spirit/Son identification with invited groups, response conditions, and suffering that do not occur anywhere in the selected section. Likewise, the lexical record includes διψυχεῖν and describes repentance opportunities and their acceptance, although this unit contains neither that verb nor that discussion. The supplemental report locates those subjects in preceding Similitude 8 units, not here. These are inaccurate unit-level source claims, even though the reader text does not import them.
findings.suggested_revision: Remove or relocate the preceding-unit material. Limit this unit’s theological decision to its Spirit/Son identification and other claims actually present here; limit its repentance lexical entry to μετανοίας in “angel of repentance.” Retain any broader historical audit material with an explicit cross-unit label.

findings.source_quote: ὅτε οὖν ἐνεδυναμώθης διὰ τοῦ πνεύματος καὶ ἴσχυσας τῇ ἰσχύϊ σου, ὥστε δύνασθαί σε καὶ ἄγγελον ἰδεῖν
findings.english_quote: The Spirit strengthened you. When you were strong enough even to see an angel
findings.issue: Independently compared with the Greek, this omits τῇ ἰσχύϊ σου, “in your strength,” and compresses the separate growing-strong statement and its result into “strong enough.” The source’s repeated strength wording and possessive disappear.
findings.suggested_revision: Consider: “When you were strengthened through the Spirit and grew strong in your strength, you became able even to see an angel”. Review the proposed wording afresh, retaining the source’s wording without adding an explanation of how the two kinds of strengthening relate.

findings.source_quote: εἰς τοῦτο γὰρ καὶ ἐδόθην ὑπὸ τοῦ ἐνδόξου ἀγγέλου εἰς τὸν οἶκόν σου κατοικῆσαι, ἵνα δυνατῶς πάντα ἴδῃς, μηδὲν δειλαινόμενος ὡς καὶ τὸ πρότερον.
findings.english_quote: The glorious angel assigned me to live in your house for this purpose. You can then see everything with strength, without being frightened as before.
findings.issue: The independent assertion “You can then see” changes the ἵνα clause from the purpose of the assignment into a statement of resulting ability. The preceding “for this purpose” does not fully preserve that grammatical relationship.
findings.suggested_revision: Consider: “The glorious angel assigned me to live in your house so that you might see everything with strength, without being frightened as before.” Review this replacement before adoption.

findings.source_quote: οὐ λίαν δὲ ἦσαν εὐθαλεῖς αἱ βοτάναι, μᾶλλον δὲ ὡς μεμαραμέναι ἦσαν.
findings.english_quote: Plants grew in them, but looked withered rather than flourishing.
findings.issue: “Rather than flourishing” removes the qualification λίαν from “not very flourishing” and makes the negative description more categorical. The source first qualifies the degree of flourishing, then says the plants looked more like withered plants.
findings.suggested_revision: Consider: “Plants grew in them, but they were not very flourishing; instead, they looked withered.” Preserve the qualified negation in any further simplification.

findings.source_quote: Μετὰ τὸ γράψαι με τὰς ἐντολὰς καὶ παραβολὰς τοῦ ποιμένος, τοῦ ἀγγέλου τῆς μετανοίας, ἦλθε πρὸς με καὶ λέγει μοι· Θέλω σοι δεῖξαι ὅσα σοι ἔδειξε τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον τὸ λαλῆσαν μετὰ σοῦ ἐν μορφῇ τῆς Ἐκκλησίας· ἐκεῖνο γὰρ τὸ πνεῦμα ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ Θεοῦ ἐστίν.
findings.english_quote: Retain rod fractions, both invited groups, repentance conditions, suffering without supplied willingness, the Spirit/Son identification and all twelve distinct mountain descriptions; preserve substantive alternative notes.
findings.issue: The simplification metadata claims preservation of rod fractions, invited groups, repentance conditions, and suffering absent from this selected unit. Its theological metadata repeats the unrelated groups, conditions, and suffering claims, and its lexical metadata includes the absent διψυχεῖν. The supplied report associates these subjects with preceding units. Only the Spirit/Son identification and mountain descriptions in this quoted list belong here.
findings.suggested_revision: Make all three metadata blocks unit-specific. Remove or explicitly relocate the preceding-unit material; retain the Spirit/Son identification, twelve mountain descriptions, substantive alternatives, and contextual explanation of “angel of repentance.”

summary: Both editions require revision. The standard has a small source-wording omission and inaccurate cross-unit metadata; the simplified independently has those problems plus a purpose-clause shift and loss of a qualified negation. Both preserve the difficult Spirit/Son assertion, speaker attribution, contextual “repentance,” and the disclosed working angel reading. The supplied bounded reports do not establish a concrete contradiction in the substantive variant notes; editorial readings and partial restorations should remain distinguished from preserved witness text. This is a model review of the supplied source and reports, not authentication of unseen manuscripts or exhaustive collation. Proposed replacements require fresh review.
